cards.statement: Automatically recovering from failure is a design principle of the performance efficiency pillar.
cards.explanation: Automatically recovering from failure is a reliability design principle, alongside testing recovery procedures and scaling horizontally.
cards.misconception: Mixing up the reliability and performance efficiency pillars.

cards.statement: The total cost of ownership of on-premises infrastructure includes facilities, power and staff costs.
cards.explanation: On-premises costs go beyond buying servers: data center space, power and the people who rack and maintain hardware all count. In the cloud, AWS carries that heavy lifting.

cards.statement: Defining infrastructure as code with AWS CloudFormation makes environment provisioning repeatable.
cards.explanation: A CloudFormation template describes resources once and can be deployed again and again, which cuts the manual effort and human error of provisioning by hand.

cards.statement: AWS cost optimization guidance recommends measuring a workload's business output alongside its cost.
cards.explanation: The cost optimization pillar's "measure overall efficiency" principle ties spending to business output, so teams can see the gains from increasing output and reducing cost.

cards.statement: In the shared responsibility model, security "of" the cloud is the customer's responsibility.
cards.explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: the infrastructure that runs AWS services. Customers are responsible for security in the cloud, such as their data, identities and configurations.
cards.misconception: Swapping "security of the cloud" (AWS) with "security in the cloud" (customer).

cards.statement: AWS Config rules prevent noncompliant resources from being created.
cards.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations and flags noncompliant resources. Blocking an action takes a preventive control, such as a service control policy or an IAM policy.
cards.misconception: Confusing compliance assessment with preventive enforcement.

source.title: Components of an AWS Config Rule

cards.statement: AWS Audit Manager is the service that records the API calls made in an AWS account.
cards.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records API activity. AWS Audit Manager collects evidence continuously to help assess whether your controls meet compliance requirements and to prepare for audits.
cards.misconception: Confusing audit evidence collection (Audit Manager) with API activity logging (CloudTrail).

cards.statement: An on-premises deployment that uses virtualization provides most of the benefits of cloud computing.
cards.explanation: AWS describes on-premises deployment, sometimes called private cloud, as much like legacy IT: it lacks many cloud benefits, though some choose it for its dedicated resources.
cards.misconception: Assuming virtualization on its own delivers the benefits of cloud computing.

cards.statement: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides shared file storage accessed over the SMB protocol.
cards.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server offers fully managed Windows file servers reached over SMB. Amazon EFS, by contrast, uses NFS and suits Linux workloads.
services: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

source.title: What is FSx for Windows File Server?

cards.statement: Cost allocation tags appear in AWS Cost Explorer as soon as they are applied to resources.
cards.explanation: Both AWS-generated and user-defined cost allocation tags must be activated in the Billing and Cost Management console before they appear in Cost Explorer or cost reports.
cards.misconception: Assuming tags show up in cost tools without being activated.

source.title: Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags
